---
title: "Two-part models"
subtitle: "Comparing effects across two-part models with different second parts"
---

A two-part model is used when an outcome is the product of a mix of two
processes, one for observed zeroes and non-zeroes, and one for an amount among
the non-zeroes. The expected outcome is the product of the two:

$$E(y) = \Pr(y > 0) \times E(y \mid y > 0)$$

`mecompare` with `twopart` gives effects on that expected outcome and compares
them across models. The `suest2` [Two-part models](../../suest2/two-part.html)
page shows the same results with `margins`. In R, the `suest` package's
`twopart` option does this; see its
[Two-part models](../../suest_r/articles/two-part.html) page.

This example uses the medical expenditures of adults in the 2004 Medical
Expenditure Panel Survey to compare two second parts: a `glm` with a gamma
family and a log link, and Poisson pseudo-maximum likelihood (`poisson` with
robust standard errors). Both share the first part, a logit of whether a
person had any expenditures.

```{.stata-run}
. use "https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/meps", clear
(MEPS 2004 adults, total medical expenditures (from R package twopartm))

. generate byte any = exp_tot > 0

. 
. local x "c.age i.female c.lninc i.ins_unins"

. 
. quietly logit any `x', vce(robust)

. estimates store Any

. 
. quietly glm exp_tot `x' if any, family(gamma) link(log) vce(robust)

. estimates store Gamma

. 
. quietly poisson exp_tot `x' if any, vce(robust)

. estimates store Poisson

```

`twopart()` names the two pairs, each a first part and its second part; `Any`
is in both:

```{.stata-run}
. mecompare ins_unins age, models(Any Gamma Poisson) twopart(Any Gamma Any Poisson)

Predicting: Two-part mean of exp_tot
Marginal effects and cross-model differences (N_Any+Gamma=19386) (N_Any+Poisson=19386)

                                 |  ME #   Estimate  Robust SE      P>|z|
---------------------------------+---------------------------------------
ins unins                        |                                       
                       1 - 0     |                                       
                       Any+Gamma |     1  -2842.902    115.919      0.000
                     Any+Poisson |     2  -2846.425    115.111      0.000
                      Difference |     3      3.523     36.849      0.924
---------------------------------+---------------------------------------
age + 1 (centered)               |                                       
                       Any+Gamma |     4    107.110      4.947      0.000
                     Any+Poisson |     5     98.982      4.362      0.000
                      Difference |     6      8.128      2.054      0.000

```

The two models give nearly the same effect of being uninsured: expected
expenditures about $2,840 lower. The difference between them, about $4, is not
significant. The effect of a year of age is about $107 with the gamma second
part and $99 with the Poisson one, and that difference, about $8, is
significant.

A two-part model can also be compared with a single model for the outcome.
Models not named in `twopart()` keep their own prediction -- here, a Poisson
model fit to everyone, zeros included:

```{.stata-run}
. local x "c.age i.female c.lninc i.ins_unins"

. 
. quietly poisson exp_tot `x', vce(robust)

. estimates store OnePart

. 
. mecompare ins_unins age, models(Any Poisson OnePart) twopart(Any Poisson)

Predicting: Two-part mean of exp_tot (Any+Poisson), Predicted mean of exp_tot (OnePart)
Marginal effects and cross-model differences (N_Any+Poisson=19386) (N_OnePart=19386)

                                 |  ME #   Estimate  Robust SE      P>|z|
---------------------------------+---------------------------------------
ins unins                        |                                       
                       1 - 0     |                                       
                     Any+Poisson |     1  -2846.425    115.111      0.000
                         OnePart |     2  -3028.215    109.027      0.000
                      Difference |     3    181.789     13.693      0.000
---------------------------------+---------------------------------------
age + 1 (centered)               |                                       
                     Any+Poisson |     4     98.982      4.362      0.000
                         OnePart |     5    100.032      4.487      0.000
                      Difference |     6     -1.050      0.299      0.000

```

The one-part model gives a larger effect of being uninsured, about $3,030, or
about $180 more than the two-part model, and the difference is significant. The
effects of age are close, about $99 and $100, though the difference of about $1
is significant.
